articles.title: Stable 2-year migration on radiostereometric analysis and improved gait speed and function after bicruciate-retaining TKA: a prospective cohort of 25 patients.
articles.authors: Mills K, Van Laarhoven SN, Defoort KC, Susan S, Heesterbeek PJC
articles.population: Patients undergoing bicruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Component migration at 2 years (radiostereometric analysis), gait speed and stride parameters, patient-reported outcome measures, adverse events
articles.take_home: The knee implants showed good stability with minimal movement over 2 years. Patients reported meaningful improvements in quality of life after surgery, though improvements in walking speed were modest.

articles.title: Arthroplasty versus internal fixation for displaced femoral neck fractures in older patients with dementia: a target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Jensen SS, Gundtoft PH, Nelissen RGHH, Gjertsen JE, Pedersen AB
articles.study_type: Observational comparative-effectiveness study using target trial emulation framework
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and older with dementia and displaced femoral neck fracture
articles.sample_size: 3,161 patients (2,231 receiving arthroplasty, 930 receiving internal fixation)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation within 365 days (primary), major reoperation, mortality, length of stay, early mobilisation, and postoperative mobility decline
articles.take_home: Internal fixation was associated with fewer reoperations and lower mortality compared with arthroplasty in older patients with dementia and displaced femoral neck fracture. However, the study authors caution that differences in how outcomes were recorded and unmeasured confounding factors may affect these findings.

articles.title: Outcomes Following Operative Management of Distal Humerus Nonunions.
articles.authors: Harrison NJ, Yu Z, Bloomer A, Chen AT, Mir H, Babcock S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective case series from seven academic trauma centres
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over who had surgery to repair a distal humerus (upper arm bone) nonunion
articles.outcomes: Recalcitrant nonunion rate, postoperative complications, and factors associated with surgical success
articles.take_home: About one in four patients (23%) failed to achieve bone healing after surgery for distal humerus nonunion, and 43% experienced complications. Patients whose original fracture was open (where bone broke through the skin) had a higher risk of failure, but factors like age, smoking, diabetes and use of bone graft did not significantly affect outcomes.

articles.title: Femoral allograft augmentation in addition to locking plate fixation in displaced proximal humerus fractures: a retrospective case-series.
articles.authors: Kool CEM, Baas DC, Riedijk R, Kok LM
articles.population: Adults with displaced proximal humerus fractures (2-, 3- or 4-part fractures)
articles.outcomes: Range of motion (anteflexion, external rotation, internal rotation, abduction), humeral head height, humeral neck shaft angle, and complications including infection and avascular necrosis
articles.take_home: Adding cancellous bone from a donor femur to locking plate surgery for displaced shoulder fractures showed good movement and stable bone position in this small group of 14 patients. There were three serious complications including two infections and one case of bone death.

articles.title: Radiographic union rate and predictors of nonunion after primary surgical implant generation network intramedullary nailing for open tibial shaft fractures at a major trauma center in Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Enquahone SA, Tekle AN, Assefa SW, Tesfaye DA, Agegnehu MB, Lapiso TH, et al.
articles.population: Patients with open tibial shaft fractures (Gustilo-Anderson grade I to IIIA) treated at a trauma centre in Ethiopia
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union rate was 89.7% (78 of 87 patients). Nonunion was more likely with severe fractures (grade IIIA), postoperative infection, and surgery delayed beyond 48 hours.
articles.take_home: Most patients with open tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nailing healed successfully, but infections, severe fractures, and delays in surgery increased the risk of healing failure. Early surgery and careful infection prevention are important for good outcomes.

articles.title: Early to mid-term outcomes of the custom-made 3D-printed triflange acetabular component (aMace) : the largest UK dual-centre study.
articles.authors: Khaled AS, Khaliq M, Barrow J, Kwaees TA, Shah N, Wynn Jones H, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision hip arthroplasty for massive acetabular bone loss
articles.sample_size: 52 patients from two UK revision centres
articles.outcomes: Component survival, reoperation rates, complications (dislocation, fracture, nerve palsy), leg length discrepancy, pain and mobility scores
articles.take_home: The aMace custom 3D-printed acetabular component showed good mid-term results with no components needing revision and low complication rates (5.7% reoperation rate) over a median follow-up of 51 months. Patients experienced significant improvements in pain and mobility, supporting use of this implant in specialist centres for severe acetabular bone loss.

articles.title: Is the use of Porous Threaded Titanium Implants Associated with Lower Rates of Implant Migration in Elderly Pelvic Ring Injuries?
articles.authors: Collins AP, Caruso B, Rockov ZA, Kleweno CP, Firoozabadi R
articles.population: Older adults aged 65 years and over with pelvic ring injuries treated with surgery
articles.sample_size: 271 patients (215 with standard steel screws, 56 with porous threaded titanium implants)
articles.outcomes: Implant movement of 2mm or more on X-rays, need for revision surgery, and changes to weight bearing restrictions
articles.take_home: Porous threaded titanium implants showed no movement compared to 18% movement with standard steel screws in older people with pelvic injuries. However, this did not significantly reduce the need for further surgery or changes to weight bearing advice.

articles.title: Development of a therapist-supervised flexibility and resistance exercise intervention for adults aged 50 years and over with a distal radius fracture in the Wrist Injury Strengthening Exercise (WISE) trial.
articles.authors: Sheehan W, Lamb SE, Forde CP, Srikesavan C, Nicolson PJA, Tutton E, et al.
articles.study_type: Intervention development study using MRC guidance, with embedded feasibility RCT
articles.population: Adults aged 50 years and over with a distal radius fracture
articles.outcomes: Feasibility of two delivery methods; therapist and patient feedback on intervention content, progression and materials
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a wrist fracture rehabilitation programme based on guidelines, research, and feedback from therapists and patients. A feasibility study showed that supervised sessions with a therapist worked better than a single session approach, leading to a final programme of up to three one-to-one therapy sessions plus a workbook with exercises and self-management advice.

articles.title: Effect of blood transfusion on respiratory failure in severe trauma patients: A post hoc analysis of a randomized multicenter trial in Japan.
articles.authors: Tanaka C, Tagami T, Fukuda R, Sakamoto T, Nakayama F, Kuno M
articles.study_type: Post hoc analysis of a randomised multicenter trial
articles.population: Adult severe trauma patients with severe bleeding or suspected severe bleeding and circulatory shock transferred to emergency department
articles.outcomes: Respiratory failure within 7 days after admission
articles.take_home: Among severe trauma patients, higher volumes of platelet transfusion in the first 24 hours were associated with increased risk of respiratory failure within a week. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusions were not linked to respiratory failure.

articles.title: Bacterial cellulose-sericin gold nanoparticle conduit functionalized with GDNF for peripheral nerve regeneration: An experimental sciatic nerve injury model in rats.
articles.authors: Maral F, Yasinoglu N, Icbudak F, Cevik S, Unal S, Karaca BT, et al.
articles.population: Wistar rats with sciatic nerve injury
articles.outcomes: Gait analysis, electromyography measurements, axon diameter, myelin sheath thickness, vessel count, and histological analysis at 8 weeks
articles.take_home: A new nerve conduit made from bacterial cellulose with gold nanoparticles and a growth factor called GDNF produced healing results in rats' injured nerves that were comparable to traditional nerve grafts taken from the animals' own tissue.

articles.title: Profound motorcycle risks: a national mileage exposure-adjusted analysis.
articles.authors: Pottayil F, Rider DE, Parry JA, Large TM
articles.population: Adults aged 18 to 80 years admitted to trauma centres in the United States after motorcycle or motor vehicle crashes
articles.sample_size: 1,419,094 admissions (334,310 motorcycle crashes, 1,084,784 motor vehicle crashes)
articles.outcomes: Admission rate, intensive care unit admission, amputation, in-hospital mortality, injury severity, head and neck injury, open long-bone fracture, and ventilation requirements per 100 million vehicle miles travelled
articles.take_home: Motorcycle crashes cause far more severe injuries and deaths than car crashes when adjusted for how many miles are ridden or driven. For every 100 million miles, motorcyclists were 43 times more likely to be admitted to hospital, 183 times more likely to need amputation, and 52 times more likely to die than car drivers.

articles.title: Beyond the Operating Room: Orthopaedic Advocacy, Identity, and Wider Impact.
articles.authors: Salphale YS, Babhulkar SS, Salphale AY
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons
articles.outcomes: Role of orthopaedic surgeons in advocacy, education, systems improvement, disability inclusion, and health policy beyond operative care
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic surgeons may have responsibility to contribute to advocacy, education and policy work alongside clinical surgery, provided this multiplies benefit for patients and communities rather than simply reducing operating capacity. The ethical consideration is whether such wider roles strengthen or weaken the overall delivery of musculoskeletal care.

articles.title: Plasma calprotectin as infection biomarker in hip fracture patients: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Pyrhonen HS, Tham J, Stefansdottir A, Persson A, Malmgren L, Rogmark C
articles.population: Hip fracture patients aged 65 years and over treated with surgery
articles.outcomes: Any infection within 30 days and 7 days after surgery; comparison of diagnostic performance of plasma calprotectin, procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, and white blood cell count measured on postoperative day 3
articles.take_home: Plasma calprotectin showed better performance than some other blood markers (procalcitonin and C-reactive protein) at detecting infections after hip fracture surgery, particularly for infections occurring within 7 days, though it provided only moderate accuracy overall. The white blood cell count performed similarly to calprotectin.

articles.title: Alcohol use is common in older patients with fall-related fractures: a secondary analysis from a prospective cohort study using PEth as an objective assessment of consumption.
articles.authors: Rogmark C, Malmgren L, Holmgren A, Magnusson A, Pyrhonen HS
articles.population: Older adults aged 65 years and over admitted to hospital after a fall-related fracture
articles.outcomes: Alcohol consumption measured by phosphatidylethanol (PEth) biomarker; association with frailty status, hyponatraemia, and 90-day mortality
articles.take_home: One in five older patients with fall-related fractures have ongoing alcohol consumption. Patients with ongoing alcohol use were more likely to develop low blood sodium, but no other major short-term harms were identified.

articles.title: Harnessing the potential of response surface methodology-based optimized scaffolds in volumetric muscle loss repair in sprague dawley rat.
articles.authors: Kumar S, Iyer VA, Verma YK
articles.population: Sprague-Dawley rats with volumetric muscle loss
articles.outcomes: Muscle fibre development, collagen deposition, and gene expression (MyoD and STAT3) at 21 days
articles.take_home: A specially designed scaffold containing collagen, fibronectin and raloxifene significantly improved muscle repair in rats with large muscle injuries. The optimized scaffold promoted new muscle fibre growth and tissue healing.

articles.title: Acellular fish-skin grafting complex soft tissue defects in orthopedic trauma: Technique and outcomes of a consecutive case series.
articles.authors: Kallevang JK, Faherty MS, Scheschuk J
articles.population: Adult patients with complex extremity wounds from traumatic injury, wound breakdown, soft tissue infection, or bone infection
articles.outcomes: Complete wound healing without flap reconstruction; number of graft applications; duration of negative-pressure wound therapy; time to split-thickness skin grafting; complications
articles.take_home: Fish-skin grafts helped 84% of patients with complex wounds heal without needing flap surgery, even those with exposed bone or tendons. This may be a useful option for patients who cannot have reconstructive surgery or in hospitals without plastic surgery services.

articles.title: Comparative study of autologous bone graft and bone morphogenetic protein-2 for bone regeneration using a novel rabbit Masquelet technique model.
articles.authors: Yamamoto Y, Fukui T, Kumabe Y, Sawauchi K, Yoshikawa R, Takase K, et al.
articles.population: New Zealand White rabbits aged 24 weeks
articles.outcomes: Bone union rate, cortical continuity, bone volume, tissue mineral density, and biomechanical strength (ultimate stress, stiffness, failure energy)
articles.take_home: BMP-2 delivered on a bone substitute material produced similar bone healing to autologous bone graft in this rabbit model, suggesting it could be a useful alternative that avoids the pain and complications associated with harvesting bone from the patient's own pelvis.

articles.title: Oxidative stress in osteoarthritis: From mitochondrial homeostasis to targeted delivery systems.
articles.authors: Zhang Q, Li Q
articles.population: Osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Molecular mechanisms of oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in osteoarthritis; effectiveness of targeted drug delivery systems including ROS-responsive hydrogels, nanocarriers, and exosome platforms
articles.take_home: Oxidative stress and mitochondrial damage drive osteoarthritis progression, but new drug delivery systems such as smart hydrogels and nanoparticles could help get antioxidant treatments to the joint more effectively and keep them working longer.

articles.title: Prognostic factors and visual outcomes in badminton-related ocular injuries: A retrospective study.
articles.authors: Tara D, Agrawal R, Hoskin A, Natarajan R, Thigale UY, Vuyyuru S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with badminton-related eye injuries presenting to an eye clinic in India
articles.outcomes: Final best corrected visual acuity, comparison of actual visual outcomes with Ocular Trauma Score predictions, identification of prognostic factors
articles.take_home: Most badminton eye injuries are from being hit by the shuttlecock and result in closed-globe injuries with generally favourable visual outcomes, though several factors including initial vision, lens damage and optic nerve involvement affect prognosis. No players were wearing protective eyewear, highlighting the importance of eye protection when playing badminton.

articles.title: Pre-hospital pulse pressure as an early predictor of active hemorrhage in trauma patients.
articles.authors: Czarnecka Z, McCluskey S, Nadolski N, Ball CG, Inaba K, Cowan S, et al.
articles.population: Adult trauma patients at level 1 trauma centres in Alberta, Canada
articles.outcomes: Ability of prehospital pulse pressure to predict active haemorrhage requiring surgery, interventional radiology, or blood transfusion within 24 hours of arrival
articles.take_home: Narrowed pulse pressure measured before hospital arrival can help identify trauma patients who are actively bleeding and need urgent treatment. A pulse pressure of 45 mmHg or less is particularly useful for recognising patients at risk of serious bleeding.

articles.title: How have management and outcomes of periprosthetic proximal femoral fractures changed? A comparison of two 8 year time periods in a high volume centre.
articles.authors: Toner E, Madden-McKee C, Goodland C, Curran A, Cassidy R, Karayiannis P, et al.
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic femoral fractures following total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Incidence of fracture types, treatment methods used, time to surgery, return to pre-injury residence, mortality at 30, 90 and 12 months, re-operation rates
articles.take_home: Periprosthetic femoral fractures are becoming more common and patients are frailer, with 12-month mortality rising from 12.2% to 20%. A shift towards fixing rather than replacing fractured bones in certain fracture types appears safe and may be beneficial, particularly in frail patients, though overall outcomes remain challenging.

articles.title: Outcomes of circular frame external fixation for tibia fracture in the elderly: comparison with a fracture-matched younger cohort.
articles.authors: Akhtar H, Muir R, Al Omar H, Harwood P, Moulder E, Groom W, et al.
articles.population: Patients with tibia fractures treated with circular frame external fixation; older adults aged over 64 and younger adults aged 18-50
articles.outcomes: Rate and time to bone union, adverse events (problems, obstacles and complications), pin site infections, need for further procedures
articles.take_home: Circular frame fixation works equally well for older and younger patients with tibia fractures in terms of bone healing. Older patients are more likely to develop pin site infections and should be warned about this risk, but serious complications do not occur more often in older patients.

articles.title: Development of zein-coated Ag-NPs integrated into decellularized fish skin extracellular matrix as a hybrid scaffold for wound healing: In-vitro and in vivo study.
articles.authors: Azizipour E, Zareshahrabadi Z, Vaez A, Kamyab H, Shanmugapriya D, Yarahmadi R, et al.
articles.study_type: Laboratory and animal study (in vitro and in vivo)
articles.population: Rat models with excisional wounds
articles.outcomes: Wound healing rate, re-epithelialisation, inflammation levels, collagen organisation, antimicrobial activity against common wound bacteria and fungi, biocompatibility
articles.take_home: A new wound dressing made from fish skin material containing silver nanoparticles showed promise in laboratory and rat studies, killing bacteria and fungi whilst supporting tissue repair and achieving 90-95% wound healing by day 14. Further research in humans would be needed to confirm whether this approach could help treat infected wounds in patients.

articles.title: General anesthesia is associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation.
articles.authors: Sasaki J, Koltenyuk V, Mrazik S, Hand C, Varano M, Xu J, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national surgical database
articles.population: Frail and severely frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation surgery
articles.sample_size: 24,401 patients receiving general anesthesia and 6,193 receiving spinal anesthesia
articles.outcomes: Mortality, unplanned readmission, and overall complications within 30 days of surgery
articles.take_home: In frail patients having hip fracture surgery, general anesthesia was linked to higher rates of death, readmission to hospital, and complications compared with spinal anesthesia. Spinal anesthesia may be a safer choice for frail patients, or if general anesthesia is used, closer monitoring after surgery may help prevent problems.

articles.title: The impact of socioeconomic deprivation on outcomes following open upper-limb fractures.
articles.authors: Tan YC, Teo BBL, Beale H, Asaad O, Hettiaratchy S, Reilly P, et al.
articles.population: Patients with open fractures of the upper limb (humerus, radius, ulna, scapula, or clavicle) treated at a Level I Major Trauma Centre
articles.outcomes: Time to surgical debridement, length of stay, 30-day and 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, and postoperative infection
articles.take_home: Patients from more deprived areas presented in poorer health and with more severe fracture grades, but after accounting for these differences, deprivation was not independently linked to delays in surgery or worse early outcomes. Standardised trauma care may help reduce health inequalities in upper-limb fracture outcomes.

articles.title: Treatment and outcome of proximal femur fractures in a resource limited setting: a prospective observational study in rural Tanzania.
articles.authors: Eleveld AJ, Mtui GS, Hendriks TCC, Bellet FD, Botman M, Bloemers FW, et al.
articles.population: Patients admitted with proximal femur fractures in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania
articles.outcomes: One-year mortality, disability (Harris Hip Score and WHODAS 2.0), quality of life (EQ-5D-3L)
articles.take_home: Most patients with hip fractures in this rural Tanzanian hospital were treated without surgery, resulting in poor outcomes. One in four patients died within a year, and only about one third recovered to their pre-injury level of function.

articles.title: Socioeconomic impact of upper and lower extremity fractures among temporary migrant workers: A prospective longitudinal cohort study.
articles.authors: Lari A, Mohammad H, Bahbahani R, Alenezi N, AlQattan A, Alherz M
articles.population: Temporary migrant workers in Kuwait aged 18-65 years with arm or leg fractures
articles.outcomes: Income changes at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months after fracture; complete income loss; return to work rates; income retention compared to baseline
articles.take_home: Nearly a quarter of temporary migrant workers had lost all income 12 months after breaking an arm or leg, with many who did return to work earning less than before. Self-employed workers and those with multiple fractures were particularly badly affected financially.

articles.title: Effect of AI-assisted radiographic fracture detection on paediatric emergency department length of stay through fracture exclusion: A before-after cohort study.
articles.authors: Graif N, Ovadia D, Rachevsky G, Kazum E, Sandler A, Goetz M, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric patients presenting to emergency department with suspected fractures during standard working hours
articles.sample_size: 4172 fracture-excluded patients (2514 pre-AI, 1658 post-AI) and 1155 fracture-confirmed patients
articles.outcomes: Emergency department length of stay, orthopaedic consultation rates, 30-day re-admission rates
articles.take_home: An artificial intelligence tool helped doctors confidently rule out fractures, reducing emergency department time by 28 minutes for patients who did not need orthopaedic referral. The tool did not change outcomes for patients with confirmed fractures, suggesting it specifically helped with fracture exclusion.

articles.title: The Role of Biological Age in Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery.
articles.authors: Salazar LM, Vaja S, Samartzis D, Lee NJ
articles.population: Adults with spinal deformity undergoing surgery
articles.outcomes: Perioperative morbidity, discharge disposition, proximal junctional failure, implant fracture, pseudarthrosis
articles.take_home: How well someone recovers from adult spinal deformity surgery depends more on their biological health markers like muscle strength and bone quality than on their age alone. Using these biological markers to assess risk before surgery helps doctors plan safer, more personalised treatment for each patient.
